messages:
anya: quick heads-up — merchant finetune merged for customer 'SolsticePay' shows weird token fingerprint mismatch after LoRA merge + int4 quant. extraction tasks replace vendor names with <unk> intermittently.

bryce: ugh. tokenizer mismatch or merge bug? any tiny repro we can run locally?

anya: repro command I used: `./dev/eval/run_pack.sh solstice_merchant_150 --model merged_solsticepay_lora --quant int4`

anya: minimal example pasted inline:
```
INPUT: \"Invoice
Vendor: Solstice Energy Co.
Amount: $1,234.00\"
FP16: \"Vendor: Solstice Energy Co.\"
INT4: \"Vendor: <unk> Energy Co.\"
TOKEN DIFF: \"Solstice\" -> id 214 fp16, id 217 int4-run (post-merge)
```

li: that looks like a deterministic id offset for a token bucket. Did the finetune metadata include the tokenizer build hash?

anya: finetune metadata: tokenizer_fingerprint: spm-20230112-a0f, base model tokenizer_fingerprint: spm-20230430-b7c. So different builds.

nate: Two recovery paths: (1) remap LoRA delta indices to base tokenizer ids at merge time (fast, non-intrusive), (2) retokenize finetune training data and retrain LoRA (clean, but slower and customer-impacting).

anya: I tried a remap run: `tools/tokenmap/rebase_lora.py --lora lora_solsticepay.pt --map spm_a0f_to_b7c.json --out lora_solsticepay_remap.pt` — script completes. Requesting evals. @eval-bot can you queue solstice_merchant_150 for fp16, int4_raw, int4_remapped on staging?

eval-bot: queued run 5178900025: solstice_merchant_150 on merged_solsticepay fp16, int4_raw, int4_remapped. ETA ~9m. Results will appear in /runs/5178900025.

bryce: while we wait, quick thought: quant may change alignment if token ids get shifted across embedding-block boundaries (e.g., groupings used by quant kernels). Need to verify reindexing correctly updates any block-level packing metadata.

li: good point. I checked the rebase tool — it rewrites embedding rows by new index but doesn't touch quant-block headers. If quant kernel expects contiguous blocks of 128 tokens, a +3 shift could slide tokens into different block buckets. We should validate block alignment for quant deployment.

nate: interim results from staging UI (summary): fp16 EM=0.90, int4_raw EM=0.52, int4_remapped EM=0.86. Token-overlap heatmap shows a contiguous id bucket shifted by +3 pre-remap, matching the spm diffs. Remap restores most vendor surface strings. Remaining failures are rare vendor aliases (e.g., \"Solstice-Pay\" vs \"Solstice Pay\") that were split differently between builds.

anya: actionable plan I propose: 1) add an automatic tokenizer_fingerprint check during LoRA merge and fail fast if mismatched without an explicit --allow-remap flag, 2) add remap step in merge pipeline that updates embedding indices and quant-block metadata, 3) add a small calibration step that optionally runs 100-step weight nudge on remapped ids to reduce residual degradation, 4) add adversarial 40-sample subset to solstice_merchant pack covering common aliasing / hyphenation patterns.

bryce: +1. Also add a console/PR message recommending customers produce finetunes with the same spm build or provide their tokenizer artifact. Update onboarding doc for SEs.

li: I'll modify the rebase tool to also patch quant-block headers and emit a small verification report (block_id -> token_ids mapping). I'll add unit tests for edge-case alias splits.

anya: I'll open PR with: remap-in-merge, optional calibration flag `--calibrate-ids`, gating on tokenizer_fingerprint mismatch, and the adversarial vectors. Will attach repro command and staging run id 5178900025.

nate: For the calibration step, suggest we do a light L2-fit on deltas for remapped indices using a small heldout validation set (customer-provided or synthetic). That should be quick (few minutes) and might recover the last few percent.

bryce: consider adding a warning in Redwood Console when uploading a LoRA that tokenizer_fingerprint differs from model catalog entry. Preferably with a link to remap docs.

anya: Agreed. I'll draft the console warning text. Also will add a short checklist entry: \"Tokenizer fingerprint parity confirmed or remap.json provided.\"

eval-bot: run 5178900025 complete: detailed results at /runs/5178900025. Artifacts: diff heatmap, per-template failure list, remap_log.txt.

anya: pulled the artifacts: remap recovered EM to 0.86 but calibration boosted it to 0.89 in a quick follow-up. The calibration script: `tools/tokenmap/calibrate_remap.py --lora lora_remap.pt --valset solstice_alias_40.json --out lora_remap_cal.pt` — small fit over 40 samples.

li: that suggests calibration is worth offering as opt-in. We should default to remap+calibrate when tokenizer mismatch detected, unless user explicitly opts out.

bryce: :thumbsup: Also log the exact tokenizer diff summary in the merge artifact so support can triage customer tickets faster.

anya: I'll include the merge artifact bundle and update the onboarding docs + add the regression test that asserts EM_drop(fp16 -> int4_remap_cal) <= 0.05 for solstice packs. PR incoming.

sara: quick note from SEs: customers will prefer a fast remap rather than retraining. Let's make the UX clear and reversible.

anya: yup — remap artifacts will be stored and merge will be reversible in case customer wants a full retrain. I'll ping once PR is up.

bryce: thanks team. nice catch.
